units.text: INT. EARNEST - CONTINUOUS
Seizes hold of Algernon.

Dr. Chasuble, my unfortunate brother. Miss Prism, my unfortunate brother. Gwendolen, my unfortunate brother. Algy, you young scoundrel, you will have to treat me with more respect in the future. You have never behaved to me like a brother in all your life.
units.name: JACK

units.text: Well, not till to-day, old boy, I admit. I did my best, however, though I was out of practice.
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: Shakes hands.
To Jack.
My own! But what own are you? What is your Christian name, now that you have become some one else?
units.name: GWENDOLEN

units.text: Good heavens! . . . I had quite forgotten that point. Your decision on the subject of my name is irrevocable, I suppose?
units.name: JACK

units.text: I never change, except in my affections.
units.name: GWENDOLEN

units.text: What a noble nature you have, Gwendolen!
units.name: CECILY

units.text: Then the question had better be cleared up at once. Aunt Augusta, a moment. At the time when Miss Prism left me in the hand-bag, had I been christened already?
units.name: JACK

units.text: Every luxury that money could buy, including christening, had been lavished on you by your fond and doting parents.
units.name: LADY BRACKNELL

units.text: Then I was christened! That is settled. Now, what name was I given? Let me know the worst.
units.name: JACK

units.text: Being the eldest son you were naturally christened after your father.
units.name: LADY BRACKNELL

units.text: Irritably.
Yes, but what was my father’s Christian name?
units.name: JACK

units.text: Meditatively.

I cannot at the present moment recall what the General’s Christian name was. But I have no doubt he had one. He was eccentric, I admit. But only in later years. And that was the result of the Indian climate, and marriage, and indigestion, and other things of that kind.
units.name: LADY BRACKNELL

units.text: Algy! Can’t you recollect what our father’s Christian name was?
units.name: JACK

units.text: My dear boy, we were never even on speaking terms. He died before I was a year old.
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: His name would appear in the Army Lists of the period, I suppose, Aunt Augusta?
units.name: JACK

units.text: The General was essentially a man of peace, except in his domestic life. But I have no doubt his name would appear in any military directory.
units.name: LADY BRACKNELL

units.text: The Army Lists of the last forty years are here. These delightful records should have been my constant study.
units.name: JACK

units.text: Rushes to bookcase and tears the books out.

M. Generals . . . Mallam, Maxbohm, Magley, what ghastly names they have—Markby, Migsby, Mobbs, Moncrieff! Lieutenant 1840, Captain, Lieutenant-Colonel, Colonel, General 1869, Christian names, Ernest John.
units.name: JACK

units.text: Puts book very quietly down and speaks quite calmly.
I always told you, Gwendolen, my name was Ernest, didn’t I? Well, it is Ernest after all. I mean it naturally is Ernest.
units.name: JACK

units.text: Yes, I remember now that the General was called Ernest, I knew I had some particular reason for disliking the name.
units.name: LADY BRACKNELL

units.text: Ernest! My own Ernest! I felt from the first that you could have no other name!
units.name: GWENDOLEN

units.text: Gwendolen, it is a terrible thing for a man to find out suddenly that all his life he has been speaking nothing but the truth. Can you forgive me?
units.name: JACK

units.text: I can. For I feel that you are sure to change.
units.name: GWENDOLEN

units.text: My own one!
units.name: JACK

units.text: To Miss Prism.
Lætitia!
units.name: CHASUBLE

units.text: Embraces her.
Enthusiastically.
Frederick! At last!
units.name: MISS PRISM

units.text: Cecily!
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: Embraces her.
At last!
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: Gwendolen!
units.name: JACK

units.text: Embraces her.
At last!
units.name: JACK

units.text: My nephew, you seem to be displaying signs of triviality.
units.name: LADY BRACKNELL

units.text: On the contrary, Aunt Augusta, I’ve now realised for the first time in my life the vital Importance of Being Earnest.
units.name: JACK

units.text: TABLEAU
